terms.meaning: The number of unit squares that cover a region, measured in square units.
The straight distance from a vertex to the opposite side, at right angles to it. It may fall outside the triangle.

items.name: Rectangle and square
items.example: 9 cm by 4 cm has area 36 cm². A square of side 6 cm also has area 36 cm².

items.name: Triangle
items.example: Base 10 cm and height 6 cm: 1/2 × 10 × 6 = 30 cm²

items.name: Parallelogram
items.example: Base 8 cm and height 5 cm: 8 × 5 = 40 cm²

items.name: Trapezium
items.example: Parallel sides 7 cm and 5 cm, height 4 cm: 1/2 × 4 × 12 = 24 cm²

items.name: Any polygon
items.formula: Divide it into triangles and add their areas
items.example: A quadrilateral with a diagonal of 22 cm and heights 5 cm and 3 cm on it: 55 + 33 = 88 cm²

items.name: Path around a rectangle
items.example: Outer 12 m by 8 m, inner 10 m by 6 m: 96 − 60 = 36 m²

items.name: Same base and same height
items.example: Moving the top vertex along a line parallel to the base keeps the area the same.

items.name: Diagonals of a rectangle
items.formula: They make 4 triangles of equal area
items.example: A rectangle of area 60 cm² gives 4 triangles of 15 cm².

mistakes.text: Do not forget the 1/2 for a triangle, a rhombus or a trapezium.
Use the height at right angles to the base, not the slanting side. A parallelogram's area uses its height.
A bigger perimeter does not mean a bigger area. 1 by 10 has perimeter 22 and area 10, while 5 by 5 has perimeter 20 and area 25.
Square units convert with the square of the factor. 1 m = 100 cm, but 1 m² = 10000 cm².
